newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: POSCO sees '96 net down to 640 bln won.
newsitem.headline: POSCO sees '96 net down to 640 bln won.

text.p: Pohang Iron and Steel Co (POSCO), South Korea's largest steelmaker, forecast its net profit would fall to 640 billion won on 8.4 trillion won of sales in calendar 1996 due to a drop in product prices, a senior company official said on Friday.
POSCO posted a 840 billion won in net profit on a 8.2 trillion won turnover last year.
Hwang Tae-hyun, director of the finance division, speaking at a UBS Securities Investor Forum, said net earnings growth would be flat but sales would grow to 8.8 trillion won in 1997.
In the year 2000, Hwang forecast POSCO would generate one trillion won net on a 10 trillion won turnover.
He said the company would upgrade product mix, emphasing more high-end products including cold-rolled sheet and stainless steel.
Hwang said the expansion of steel production facilites would also enable POSCO to post huge net profit in the year.
He said POSCO was aiming to expand its output to 28 million tonnes of steel products a year by 1999 against 24 million tonnes at present.
"We plan to be the number one steel producer in the world by 1999," Hwang said.
POSCO is the world's number two steelmaker at present.
